## Hydrodynamics water levels quality checking

This document is for checking that our hydrodynamic model that represents a realistic scenario for 2023 is realistically predicting water levels.

Our input water levels are from Picnic Point, and we also have water level data from 5 other stations which we will use for quality checking:

-   Dunethin Rock

-   Stoney Wharf

-   David Low Way

-   Vee road

-   Yandina Coolum road Solar Farm

![](data:image/png;base64,){alt="Untitled picture  Ink Drawings Ink Drawings Ink Drawings Ink Drawings Ink Drawings "}

In addition to these permanent stations, we also have data from water loggers that were placed within our wetland creeks of interest:

-   1A upstream

-   1A downstream

-   1B

-   West Coolum Boat Ramp

![](images/clipboard-2119549007.png)

Functions

```{r Functions}
read.csv.rma <- function(run_number, filename){
  read.csv(here(str_c("Data/WaterLevel/RMA_outputs/run", run_number, "/", filename, ".csv")), skip = 3, col.names = c("Time", "Elevation", "NA")) %>% select("Time", "Elevation")
}

Select_Logger <- function(dataset){
  dataset %>% select(c("Date Time", "Level (m AHD)")) %>% 
    rename(Time = `Date Time`, 
           WaterLevel = `Level (m AHD)`) %>% 
    mutate(Time = as.POSIXct(Time, tz = "UTC"))
}

Select_PermStation <- function(dataset){
  dataset %>% select(c("Date", "Water.Level..m.AHD.")) %>% 
    rename(Time = Date,
           WaterLevel = `Water.Level..m.AHD.`) %>% 
    mutate(Time = as.POSIXct(Time, format = "%d %b %Y %H:%M", tz = "UTC")) # recode as date
}

TimeFormatModelData <- function(dataset){ # recode as date
  dataset %>% mutate(Time = as.POSIXct(Time, format = "%d/%m/%Y %H:%M", tz = "UTC"))
}

SubsetTimes <- function(dataset){ # make a function for subsetting dates
  dataset %>% filter(between(Time, as.POSIXct("2023-01-15 00:00:00", tz = "UTC"), as.POSIXct("2023-06-02 00:00:00", tz = "UTC")))
}
```

## 2. Select relevant variables

Create functions to select only relevant variables for datasets with similar patterns. Also recode date/time variables as such (rather than as a character).

```{r Select_variables_fns}
Select_Logger <- function(dataset){
  dataset %>% select(c("Date Time", "Level (m AHD)")) %>% 
    rename(Time = `Date Time`, 
           WaterLevel = `Level (m AHD)`) %>% 
    mutate(Time = as.POSIXct(Time, tz = "UTC"))
}

Select_PermStation <- function(dataset){
  dataset %>% select(c("Date", "Water.Level..m.AHD.")) %>% 
    rename(Time = Date,
           WaterLevel = `Water.Level..m.AHD.`) %>% 
    mutate(Time = as.POSIXct(Time, format = "%d %b %Y %H:%M", tz = "UTC")) # recode as date
}

TimeFormatModelData <- function(dataset){ # recode as date
  dataset %>% mutate(Time = as.POSIXct(Time, format = "%d/%m/%Y %H:%M", tz = "UTC"))
}
```

## 3. Clip data to equivalent timeframes

-   Should ideally be two weeks or later into the model, because apparently it can take a couple weeks for the model to "fill" with water and stabilise water levels. Within 15 Jan - 2 Mar 2023.

-   Clip all datasets to this time period (note that some may not cover the whole time period)

```{r Subset_dates}
SubsetTimes <- function(dataset){ # make a function for subsetting dates
  dataset %>% filter(between(Time, as.POSIXct("2023-01-01 00:00:00", tz = "UTC"), as.POSIXct("2023-06-02 00:00:00", tz = "UTC")))
}
# listing UTC as the timezone as if we list Australia/Sydney as the timezone, it writes the equivalent UTC times anyway
```

## 4. Merge datasets at the same location

To merge datasets, we will need to join based on similar date/time. Unfortunately, the times don't exactly line up, so given our model data are recorded every 15 mins, let's join based on a 15 min window of similarity (i.e., if two date/times from different datasets are within 15 mins of one another, they are considered more or less the same and are joined so that their water level observations can be compared)

First, create a function to join and compare water level datasets.

```{r Function_join_datasets}
compare_WL_values <- function(RealData, ModelData, WaterLevelVarReal, WaterLevelVarModel, Title){
# rolling join using data.table package
# add extra Time columns
dt1 <- as.data.table(RealData) %>% mutate(Time_x = Time)
dt2 <- as.data.table(ModelData) %>% mutate(Time_y = Time)
setkey(dt1, Time)
setkey(dt2, Time)

 # Perform a rolling join to find the nearest match
 # roll = "nearest" finds the closest match, regardless of before/after
result_dt <- dt2[dt1, roll = "nearest"]

p <- ggplot(result_dt, aes(x = result_dt[[WaterLevelVarReal]], y = result_dt[[WaterLevelVarModel]])) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1) +
  ggtitle(Title)

ggsave(filename = here(str_c("Output/CompareWLGraphs/", Title, ".png")), device = "png", plot = p, width = 1000, height = 500, units = "px")
}
# have to input the two column variables as strings for this to work.
```

Next, run this function for all locations.

```{r WaterLevelCompare}
compare_WL_values(Downstream_1A, M_Downstream_1A, "WaterLevel", "Elev_695", "Downstream 1A")

compare_WL_values(Upstream_1A, M_Upstream_1A, "WaterLevel", "Elev_595", "Upstream 1A")

compare_WL_values(Dunethin, M_Dunethin, "WaterLevel", "Elevation", "Dunethin Rock")

compare_WL_values(Solonist_1B, M_1B, "WaterLevel", "Elevation", "1B Solonist")

compare_WL_values(Heron_maybe_1B, M_1B, "WaterLevel", "Elevation", "1B Heron")

compare_WL_values(Stoney, M_StoneyWharf, "WaterLevel", "Elevation", "Stoney Wharf")

compare_WL_values(WestCoolumBoatRamp, M_WestCoolumBoatRamp, "WaterLevel", "Elevation", "West Coolum Boat Ramp")

## Also run for late 2024 if we have any real data as that's when Vee Road and Solar Farm have data
```

Also, compare water level phases by plotting both datasets against time for each location. Given there are many tides over our dataset, let's subset and check phase over a shorter time period (e.g., 1 week).

Again, first create a function.

```{r WaterLevelPhaseFunction}
compare_WL_phase <- function(RealData, ModelData, ModelData2, WaterLevelVarReal, WaterLevelVarModel, WaterLevelVarModel2, Title){
# rolling join using data.table package
# add extra Time columns
dt1 <- as.data.table(RealData) %>% mutate(Time_x = Time)
dt2 <- as.data.table(ModelData) %>% mutate(Time_y = Time)
dt3 <- as.data.table(ModelData2) %>% mutate(Time_z = Time,
                                            Elevation_z = Elevation)
setkey(dt1, Time)
setkey(dt2, Time)
setkey(dt3, Time)

 # Perform a rolling join to find the nearest match
 # roll = "nearest" finds the closest match, regardless of before/after
result_dt <- dt2[dt1, roll = "nearest"]
result_dt2 <- dt3[result_dt, roll = "nearest"]


result_dt_long <- pivot_longer(result_dt2, cols = c(WaterLevelVarReal, WaterLevelVarModel, WaterLevelVarModel2), names_to = "source", values_to = "levels") %>% 
  mutate(Time_numeric = as.numeric(Time)) %>% 
  filter(between(Time, as.POSIXct("2023-01-06 00:00:00", tz = "UTC"), as.POSIXct("2023-02-02 00:00:00", tz = "UTC")))

result_dt_long$source <- result_dt_long$source %>% factor(ordered = TRUE, levels = c(WaterLevelVarModel, WaterLevelVarModel2, WaterLevelVarReal))

p <- ggplot(result_dt_long, aes(x = Time_numeric, y = levels, color = source)) +
  #geom_point(size = 0.5) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_color_manual(labels = c("model77", "model82", "observed"), values = c("red", "yellow", "blue")) +
  scale_x_datetime(date_labels = "%d-%m-%Y") +
  ggtitle(Title) +
  xlab("Date") +
  ylab("Water Level") +
  labs(color = "") 

ggsave(filename = here(str_c("Output/CompareWLPhase/", "run0082/Phase_", Title, ".png")), device = "png", plot = p, width = 6, height = 3)
}

```

Function for just comparing one model and observed data.

```{r Phase_fn_2}
compare_WL_phase1 <- function(RealData, ModelData, WaterLevelVarReal, WaterLevelVarModel, Title){
# rolling join using data.table package
# add extra Time columns
dt1 <- as.data.table(RealData) %>% mutate(Time_x = Time)
dt2 <- as.data.table(ModelData) %>% mutate(Time_y = Time)
 
setkey(dt1, Time)
setkey(dt2, Time)
 
 # Perform a rolling join to find the nearest match
 # roll = "nearest" finds the closest match, regardless of before/after
result_dt <- dt2[dt1, roll = "nearest"]
 
result_dt_long <- pivot_longer(result_dt, cols = c(WaterLevelVarReal, WaterLevelVarModel), names_to = "source", values_to = "levels") %>% 
  mutate(Time_numeric = as.numeric(Time)) %>% 
  filter(between(Time, as.POSIXct("2023-04-12 00:00:00", tz = "UTC"), as.POSIXct("2023-04-19 00:00:00", tz = "UTC")))
 
result_dt_long$source <- result_dt_long$source %>% factor(ordered = TRUE, levels = c(WaterLevelVarModel, WaterLevelVarReal))
 
p <- ggplot(result_dt_long, aes(x = Time_numeric, y = levels, color = source)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_color_manual(labels = c("Modelled", "Observed"), values = c("red", "blue")) +
  scale_x_datetime(date_labels = "%d-%m-%Y") +
  ggtitle(Title) +
  xlab("Date") +
  ylab("Water Level")  +
  labs(color = "")
  
ggsave(filename = here(str_c("Output/CompareWLPhase/", "run0078/Phase_", Title, ".png")), device = "png", plot = p, width = 6, height = 3)
}
```

## 5. Plot observed data against one another

Plot observed data together to explore differences as we move around the estuary.

Let's do it by channel:

-   Yandina creek: picnic point, stoney wharf, 1b, 1a downstream

-   Coolum creek: picnic point, stoney wharf, west coolum boat ramp, 1a upstream

```{r calibration_compare_observed}
# yandina creek
png(here("Output/ObservedYandinaCreek.png"), width = 2400, height = 1200, units = "px")
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = PicnicPointJ, aes(x = Time, y = WaterLevel, color = "Picnic Point"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data = Stoney, aes(x = Time, y = WaterLevel, color = "Stoney Wharf"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data = Heron_maybe_1B, aes(x = Time, y = WaterLevel, color = "1b - Heron"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data = Solonist_1B, aes(x = Time, y = WaterLevel, color = "1b - Solonist"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data = Downstream_1A, aes(x = Time, y = WaterLevel, color = "Downstream 1a"), linewidth = 1) +
  xlim(as.POSIXct("2023-01-17 00:00:00", tz = "UTC"),as.POSIXct("2023-01-24 00:00:00", tz = "UTC")) +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_colour_manual(name = "Logger Locations",
                      breaks = c("Picnic Point", "Stoney Wharf", "1b - Heron", "1b - Solonist", "Downstream 1a"),
                      values = c("Picnic Point" = "red", 
                                 "Stoney Wharf" = "blue", 
                                 "1b - Heron" = "green", 
                                 "1b - Solonist" = "orange", 
                                 "Downstream 1a" = "black")) +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 30),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 36),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 36),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 30)) 
dev.off()


# coolum creek
png(here("Output/ObservedCoolumCreek.png"), width = 2400, height = 1200, units = "px")
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = PicnicPointJ, aes(x = Time, y = WaterLevel, color = "Picnic Point"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data = Stoney, aes(x = Time, y = WaterLevel, color = "Stoney Wharf"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data = WestCoolumBoatRamp, aes(x = Time, y = WaterLevel, color = "West Coolum Boat Ramp"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data = Upstream_1A, aes(x = Time, y = WaterLevel, color = "Upstream 1a"), linewidth = 1) +
  xlim(as.POSIXct("2023-01-17 00:00:00", tz = "UTC"),as.POSIXct("2023-01-24 00:00:00", tz = "UTC")) +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_colour_manual(name = "Logger Locations",
                      breaks = c("Picnic Point", "Stoney Wharf", "West Coolum Boat Ramp", "Upstream 1a"),
                      values = c("Picnic Point" = "red", 
                                 "Stoney Wharf" = "blue", 
                                 "West Coolum Boat Ramp" = "cyan", 
                                 "Upstream 1a" = "purple")) +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 30),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 36),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 36),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 30))
dev.off()
```
